findings.reason: The protected Python solution uses a sliding window with left and right pointers and a character count map. As right advances, it inserts characters into the map; while len(counts) > 2, it decrements counts[s[left]] and deletes zero-count keys while advancing left. The maximum window length right - left + 1 is tracked. The algorithm runs in O(n) time and O(1) space; no candidate is required.

Maintaining character frequency counts in a sliding window and contracting left whenever distinct key count exceeds 2 ensures every considered window contains at most 2 distinct characters, correctly finding the global maximum.

Each character enters and leaves the sliding window at most once, yielding O(n) total time. Auxiliary space is O(1) since the count map holds at most 3 distinct characters at any time for English letters. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts string s and returns the integer maximum length of a valid substring.

The approach accurately details sliding window expansion, key deletion upon zero frequency, left pointer contraction, and O(n) time / O(1) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover quadratic un-optimised restart scans, last-occurrence tracking trade-offs, character pair enumeration overhead, single-character strings, 1-2 distinct character full-string limits, and rapid multi-character oscillation handling.
